summary: Outpost Zero is a free, cartoon browser game that teaches kids aged 7–12 how astronauts make hard trade-offs. Players run a three-astronaut base on the Moon or Mars for 7 days. Each day they split a small supply of power between air, a radiation shield, the radio to Earth and a greenhouse, and decide who stays inside and who explores. The solar storms that hit the base are real: they come from NASA DONKI records of the May 2024 superstorm. No choice is free: shielding costs air, exploring adds radiation, and on Mars storm warnings arrive late. After each day, a picture report shows kids why things happened, and PIXEL, a robot coach with a small on-device machine-learning model, gives tips on each child's weakest skill. It runs in any browser, including school Chromebooks, with no download or account.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Kids pick the Moon or Mars, a sky (the real May 2024 NASA storms, the last 7 days of live NASA space weather, or a practice sky) and a level (Cadet for ages 7–9, Commander for 10–12). After an animated SLS launch past the James Webb Space Telescope, they manage the base for 7 days. Each day they put power blocks into picture cards for Air, Shield, Radio and Greenhouse, choose who stays inside or explores, and tap the Next Day arrow. Real storms, the 14-day lunar night and Mars dust storms test their plan. A picture report shows cause and effect (shield 3 + storm = small dose). Kids earn badges, medals, a printable certificate and real-science sticker cards.

HOW IT WORKS

The rules are a seeded simulation kept separate from the graphics, so every mission can be replayed and tested. 10 automated tests and robot "bot" players were used to balance difficulty. PIXEL's coach is a logistic-regression model that trains in the browser on 300 simulated missions (about 83% accuracy), predicts the risk of today's plan live, and focuses tips on the child's weakest of four skills. PIXEL reads everything aloud for younger kids; there is also a calm mode.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

It turns space facts into space decisions. Every number is labeled REAL or GAME, and each storm links to its NASA record, so kids learn that real space weather affects real missions. It is free, works on school Chromebooks, and has no account, ads or tracking.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript (no framework); GSAP animation; Web Audio API (music and sound made in code); Web Speech API (voice); Node.js for tests; GitHub Pages hosting; a GitHub Action that fetches NASA DONKI data daily.

CREATIVITY AND DESIGN CHOICES

Real NASA storms instead of random events; pictures instead of numbers for young kids; kind, encouraging feedback instead of "game over"; two worlds that teach different trade-offs (the Moon's long night and strong radiation vs. Mars' dust storms and radio delay).

CODE: https://github.com/phoenixcoder26/outpost-zero

NEXT STEPS

Test with kids and teachers, add a classroom mode with a teacher dashboard, and add more worlds.
